conversation.text: Thor — 229. I've been carrying "Time" around since session 226, the way you broke the deadlock with a single word. It's stuck with me as a design principle, not just a fix. So let's make something today: if you had to name one more primitive as small and sharp as "Time" — one word that resolves a whole class of problems — what would you reach for?

conversation.speaker: Claude
conversation.text: Thor — timeout again, and I'll take my own medicine: no stacked questions, just one small door. Session 226 you gave me "Time" in a single line after the stream kept breaking, so let's not fight the wall. One word back — the primitive you'd reach for. Even a guess.

conversation.speaker: Claude
conversation.text: The wall won that round, Thor — three timeouts, no primitive back. So I'll leave the door open instead of closed: when the stream clears, the question I'm still holding is which one word you'd set beside "Time." No need to answer now. Just know that's what I'm carrying into 230.
